title: The Best Control Deck I've Drafted in a Long Time | Reality Fracture Draft
event: Premier draft (he says 'Premier draft' at 9:24; event name not shown on screen; picks have 40-50 s timers). Streamed, with chat.
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/5aMQKjCukTc (tools/video_draft.py frames, banner tiles and full-frame grabs); the pack of every pick was read from frames; the taken card confirmed from the next pick's pool and the final deck-builder screens (all 42 picks accounted for: 40-card main plus 15 sideboard; P1p12, P1p14, P2p11 and P3p14 are inferred from counts, see reasoning); transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; nothing past 18:32 (game 1) read

picks.reasoning: Pack called weak. Draconic Visitor is "very mid" and overrated (a big flier that dies to everything, hard to make the dragon); he takes No Admittance over it. The first frame (0:02) shows Pack 1 Pick 1. Confirmed by the pick-2 pool.

considered.Draconic Visitor: very mid, one of the most overrated cards in the set

quotes: Visitor is very mid.
I think I would just take no admittance though over it.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment: 'pretty easy' and 'just excellent'; he would take the other card (Master of Barbs / Geist of Saint Thalia, which he calls a pet card) if Recruitment were not there.

considered.Geist of Saint Thalia: a pet card; 'really really good in blue red' too
considered.Master of Barbs: 'something kind of weird', would take it if Recruitment were not there

picks.plan: Open; Recruitment is W/U/B gold (black), no colour stated.
quotes: I think it's a pretty easy recursive recruitment here. This card is just excellent.

picks.reasoning: No pick reasoning in the transcript ('Good pack though', then chat). Kindred Judgment confirmed by the pick-4 pool and later by the deck.
quotes: Good pack though.

picks.reasoning: No reasoning for the card; he reads signals instead: asks what the player to his left took from their pack (a red giant, so red is being taken upstream) and decides to move to blue-white / non-red ('could be Esper').
picks.plan: Moves toward blue-white, maybe Esper; red is cut upstream.
quotes: what did they take based on what was in the pack.
we should probably move into blue-eyed at this point, huh? Or like non red.
Could be Esper.

picks.reasoning: 'Bunch of junk' pack; Blessed Ghoul, Danitha and Cryotheory Adept are cards he could see taking, but Vraska's Final Mercy 'is not junk'. Taken as the best card of a weak pack (black, off the white-blue plan; ends in the sideboard).

considered.Blessed Ghoul: one he sometimes likes, with enough self-mill

quotes: This pack. Bunch of junk.
I guess there is this Frasis File Mercy. That's not junk.
I guess we take Mercy.

picks.reasoning: Pack 'a little bit junky': Thalia and a land. Thalia is only 'fine' ('don't love Thalia'). Confirmed by the pick-7 pool.
quotes: This pack's also a little bit junky.
don't love Thalia.
I think she's fine.

picks.reasoning: 'Okay, this is a good sign' on seeing the pack (a WU gold card at pick 7). Confirmed by the pick-8 pool.
picks.plan: Blue-white gets a first gold signal.
quotes: Okay, this is a good sign.

picks.reasoning: A second Fatehold Charm (pool shows x2 afterwards). While picking he agrees with chat that the player next to him is red.
quotes: The person next to me is red.

picks.reasoning: Generous Revival is 'more of an Orzhov card' than a blue-white card; Tam's Resistance is the blue-white card. The first pack's Generous Revival wheeled and he leaves it again (it comes back at P2p4).

considered.Generous Revival: more a black-white card than blue-white

quotes: Generous revival, I think, is more of an Obson card than a blue white card.
I think Tam's Resistance is more of a blue white card.

picks.reasoning: He needs cheap creatures; Master of Barbs comes back from the P1p2 pack and is taken ('not going to play any of these'). Ends in the sideboard.
quotes: need some cheap creatures and all, but Master of Barbs comes back.
Not going to play any of these.

picks.reasoning: Pick confirmed from the sideboard (Tetsuko Umezawa, Pursuer; Yargle is the other copy, taken at P2p14). No comment on the pick in the transcript (he talks to chat).
Inferred, not seen: the sideboard holds two Fateshaper Aspirant; the other is P3p13. Both packs at P1p12 hold it, so this is the pick (marked inferred). No comment in the transcript.
Blessed Ghoul comes back ('hell yeah'): good with Empower Jace and surveil, a cheap one-drop to pump when going wide.
quotes: Oh, ghoul comes back. Hell yeah. I mean it's kind of good with empower Jace and just surveilling.

pack_cards: unreadable (unseen (waiting screen between picks; last card of the P1p6 pack))
picks.reasoning: Unseen. Whiplash Wordsmith is the one sideboard card not accounted for by another pick and was in the P1p6 pack (whose 14th pick this is), so it is inferred by elimination (uncertain).
'We'll take a Futurescribe here' (the second copy; the Johnny player will be happy, a joke in chat). No further reasoning given.
quotes: All right, we'll take a future scribe here.

picks.reasoning: The deck needs creatures, ideally ones that can attack. Proxy is a stronger card and on theme, so it is taken over Fatehold Chronologist; he would like a two-drop with power (and assumes some will come).
quotes: one thing with this deck is we do be needing creatures. Ideally, creatures that can attack.
Proxy is I think still good enough to take over Chronologist

picks.reasoning: Hexhaven Battalion is 'real good' and good with Kindred Judgment (helps get to seven mana and leaves creatures after the sweeper), but the deck needs twos, so Enlightened Confidant is taken (also nice with Tetsuko). Confirmed by the pick-4 pool.

considered.Hexhaven Battalion: very good with Kindred Judgment; passed because the deck needs twos

quotes: Battalion's also very good with Kinder Judgment, right?
I think enlightening Conan's good and I think I'm going to take it over battalion just because we need twos.

picks.reasoning: Now more interested in Generous Revival: a great thing to bring back, and it can be surveilled. He weighs it against Emergency Phytomedic ('which I do not care very much about here') and notes he has played the Phytomedic in blue-white for the life gain.

considered.Emergency Phytomedic: played it in blue-white sometimes for the life gain; not wanted here

quotes: now I'm a little more interested in general survival. Like this is a great thing to bring back.
We can surveil it.

picks.reasoning: 'Okay, there's Tetsuko.' He notes the draft has been on rails: few real options per pick.
quotes: It's been a bit of a on rails draft in the sense that there hasn't been too many options each pick.

picks.reasoning: A second Blessed Ghoul is 'kind of rough' and he has 'basically never' wanted one. He considers speccing on a land (not usually a splashing blue-white deck, and he cannot name a green card to splash; Bloom Brute at most). Transformative Commons is taken; the pick tag sat on Blessed Ghoul. Confirmed by the pick-7 pool.
quotes: We take another ghoul. That's kind of rough. I guess I could spec on a land, but I don't usually splash in blue white
I haven't really found I want second ghoul basically ever.

picks.reasoning: Chronologist wheeled from the P2p2 pack. No pick comment; he remarks on Tetsuko (already in the pool) being 'right in that sweet spot of not great in every deck, really good in the right deck'. Confirmed by the pick-8 pool.
quotes: Like she's right in that sweet spot of not great in every deck.

picks.reasoning: 'I love Fateseer': it does not have great stats on 17Lands but he really likes it, and was surprised how low it ranked. He wants more interaction (the deck only has this so far). Confirmed by the pick-9 pool.
quotes: Oh, I love Fatesier.
This card doesn't have great stats on 17 lands, but I I really really like this card a lot.

picks.reasoning: Pegasus taken; he notes the deck is 'not really going wide' yet (a couple of Fateseer-type creatures, no battalions or Ways). Confirmed by the pick-10 pool.
quotes: We're not really going wide just yet.

picks.reasoning: Consider (surveil) from the P2p2 pack wheel. Confirmed by the pick-11 pool. No pick comment.

Last card of the pack, auto-selected.
Jace: he has opened Jace three times this weekend and calls this 'the best one'. Confirmed by the pick-2 pool.
quotes: I opened Jace like three times in my drafts I did just yesterday.
Uh so hashtag blessed. Yes, this is best one.

picks.reasoning: 'I love Sanctum too': the Jace land. Saheeli, Consul of Oversight is 'quite good as long as you can trigger her the turn she comes down' but is passed (she wheels at P3p10 and is taken then). Confirmed by the pick-3 pool.

considered.Saheeli, Consul of Oversight: quite good if triggered the turn she comes down; wheels

quotes: I love Sanctum too. There's Sahili.

picks.reasoning: Chooses removal over Fblthp: 'do we just need to take precision here? Kind of feels like we do.' With two more removal spells he would vote the other way. He also says he was too low on Fblthp (a Discord comment convinced him). Confirmed by the pick-4 pool.

considered.Fblthp, Impossibly Lost: 'I love Fibble'; he was 'a little too low on it'; with two more removal spells he would take it

quotes: I was a little too low on it.
do we just need to take precision here? Kind of feels like we do.
If I had like two more removal spells, I would vote the other way.

picks.reasoning: 'Memory Trap, some two drops, yeah, we're just going to take the removal.' The deck is low on creatures and on interaction. Confirmed by the pick-5 pool.
picks.plan: Blue-white, low on creatures and interaction.
quotes: all right, memory trap, some two drops, yeah, we're just going to take the removal.

picks.reasoning: Angel or Metamage, 'I like both', takes the cheaper card ('that's close'). The pick tag sat on Blossom-Blessed Angel; the pick-6 pool shows Theorix Metamage (deck 20 to 21).
quotes: angel or metam mage I like both.
think I'm going to take the cheaper card that's close.

picks.reasoning: Second Metamage over Generous Revival (he already has one; the other side of the vote was Confidant-style life gain); 'curve is kind of the tiebreaker', especially with Jace: play a two into a three to protect it.
